title: Homemade balls and boyhood odd jobs
summary: Kids made balls from stockings and earned nickels shining faucets, shopping and shining shoes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Anyway, you mentioned ball. That just happened was one of the things I was going to talk to you about. Did the kids play ball much then?

Oh, we had ours. We used to make our balls. We used to take a stocking and rip it and just wrap it up and make a ball. We probably, sometime we put a little, a little, uh, small ball, a wooden ball or something, and then we'd wrap this thread around this ball and then sew it to keep it from, from threading. We had a way of sewing the ball. And we'd play until it would rip up and then we'd make another one. That was our balls. We didn't have any good balls or good bats. We had handy downs. Sometime a kid was able to, uh, to come up and get him something new. He might have worked around and made a few nickels and finally would buy him something. We all would use it.

Little jobs. Well, such as when I was a kid, I, I shined the brass faucets for nickel and I would shop for the neighbors and get 50 cents a week and go get all that grocery. I guess that's why I know how to cook and shop today. Because it was, I'd go for four or five of them. And of course, there was a lot of other ways, shining shoes and, uh, working in the baker shops and cleaning up this and that. If a kid really wanted to, to get along, which they did. There was a lot of little jobs. They weren't lazy. We got out and did our chores. Went to school. Sometime we had a nickel to go to school. That was our lunch. Mm-hmm. Sometime the kids, one kid would buy a pickle with his nickel and another kid would buy a piece of bread with his nickel and maybe another one would buy some. Meats were so cheap, they didn't get four or five slices of ham or sausage. And you'd have enough for you to chip in and split and go and make your sandwiches.
